source_caption:
To give Brian O’Conner a proper send-off after the tragic passing of Paul Walker, the filmmakers achieved one of the most emotionally devastating and technically seamless farewells in cinematic history. While Weta Digital used cutting-edge CGI and Walker’s own brothers as physical stand-ins to finish his remaining scenes, the final “Last Ride” sequence transcends visual effects to break the fourth wall entirely. When Brian pulls up next to Dom in a white Toyota Supra—which was actually Walker’s personal car—the film ceases to be an action blockbuster and becomes a profound, open letter of grief. As the two cars diverge at a literal fork in the road and the screen fades to a peaceful white instead of the traditional black, Vin Diesel’s final monologue isn’t a character saying goodbye to his partner; it is a deeply heartbroken man saying a final, genuine farewell to his brother.
⠀
Furious 7 (2015), directed by James Wan, starring Vin Diesel, Paul Walker, Dwayne Johnson. After defeating a ruthless international terrorist, Dominic Toretto and his crew are violently hunted by the man’s deadly older brother, forcing the makeshift family into a desperate, globe-trotting war for their survival.

source_details.synopsis: Furious 7 (also known as Fast & Furious 7) is a 2015 action film directed by James Wan and written by Chris Morgan. It is the sequel to Fast & Furious 6 (2013), a follow-up to The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift (2006), and the seventh installment in the Fast & Furious franchise. The film stars an ensemble cast including Vin Diesel, Paul Walker (in his final film role), Dwayne Johnson, Michelle Rodriguez, Tyrese Gibson, Ludacris, Jordana Brewster, Djimon Hounsou, Kurt Russell, and Jason Statham.
